items.title: 1. High-Level System Architecture
items.text: Paisa Tracker runs 100% client-side in the browser. It combines React 19, Tailwind CSS v4, Chart.js, and the native React Context API with LocalStorage persistence.

items.title: 2. Data Architecture: Where is the Main Source of Data?
items.text:
One of the most important concepts to understand and explain in Paisa Tracker is how data originates, moves, updates, and stays saved across browser refreshes.

The data architecture operates in 3 distinct tiers:

flowchart LR
    subgraph Tier1 ["Tier 1: Canonical Seed Constants"]
        C1["DEFAULT_TRANSACTIONS"]
        C2["DEFAULT_GOALS"]
        C3["DEFAULT_LOANS"]
        C4["DEFAULT_SUBSCRIPTIONS"]
        C5["DEFAULT_RECURRING_INCOMES"]
        C6["DEFAULT_CATEGORIES"]
        C7["sourceData.json"]
    end

    subgraph Tier2 ["Tier 2: In-Memory Runtime Store"]
        S1["FinanceContext.jsx (React useState)"]
        S2["Derived Metrics (useMemo)"]
    end

    subgraph Tier3 ["Tier 3: Browser Persistence"]
        LS[("Browser localStorage")]
    end

    %% Initial Boot
    LS -->|1. Try loading saved JSON| S1
    C1 & C2 & C3 & C4 & C5 & C6 -->|2. Fallback if storage is empty| S1

    %% Re-renders & Actions
    S1 -->|Compute on-the-fly| S2
    S2 -->|Feed data to UI components| UI["UI Screens & Views"]
    UI -->|User dispatches actions| S1
    S1 -->|useEffect automatically writes back| LS

items.title: Tier 1: Canonical Seed Constants (Mock Data)
items.text:
• Primary Location: src/utils/financeUtils.js (and reference figures in src/data/sourceData.json).
  • What it contains:
  • DEFAULT_TRANSACTIONS: 7 realistic Indian student transactions totaling ₹14,965 inflow, ₹2,544 outflow, and ₹12,421 net balance (Pocket Money, Stationery, Books, Food, etc.).
  • DEFAULT_GOALS: Pre-configured student goal (MacBook Air M3 - ₹90,000 target).
  • DEFAULT_LOANS: Pre-configured active loan (MacBook Air M3 No-Cost EMI - ₹60,000 principal, ₹5,000/mo EMI).
  • DEFAULT_SUBSCRIPTIONS: 5 student recurring services (Spotify Premium ₹119, Netflix ₹199, YouTube Premium ₹149, Google One ₹130, Swiggy One ₹299).
  • DEFAULT_RECURRING_INCOMES: Pre-configured student recurring inflow (Monthly Pocket Money / Allowance: ₹10,000/month, credit day: 5th).
  • DEFAULT_CATEGORIES: 7 default categories with assigned color tokens (Food, Shopping, Entertainment, Bills & Utilities, Travel, Investments, Education).
  • Purpose: Acts as the immutable baseline. When a user first opens the application or clicks "Reset to Defaults", the app seeds from these constants.

items.title: Tier 2: In-Memory Runtime Source of Truth (React Context)
items.text:
• Primary Location: src/context/FinanceContext.jsx (wrapped via FinanceProvider around App.jsx).
  • How it works:
  • FinanceProvider maintains the live state variables: transactions, goals, loans, subscriptions, recurringIncomes, categories, linkedAccounts, user, and searchQuery.
  • When the app is running, this state is the single source of truth. Every component that reads data or triggers mutations reads from and writes to this provider via the useFinance() custom hook.
  • Derived calculations (such as stats with Net Balance, categorySpending with 50/30/20 budget breakdown, totalMonthlyEmi, totalRemainingDebt, and totalMonthlyRecurringIncome) are computed on-the-fly using React's useMemo.

items.title: Tier 3: Browser Persistence Engine (LocalStorage)
items.text:
• Storage Keys:
  • paisatracker_transactions: Array of ledger entries
  • paisatracker_goals: Array of savings goals
  • paisatracker_loans: Array of loan & EMI plans
  • paisatracker_subscriptions: Array of active/paused recurring subscriptions
  • paisatracker_recurring_incomes: Array of recurring monthly inflow streams
  • paisatracker_categories: Array of active spending categories
  • paisatracker_linked_banks: Array of connected simulated bank accounts
  • paisatracker_user: User profile object ({ username, isAuthenticated })
  • paisatracker_selected_goal: Currently focused goal ID for the Adaptive Planner
  • Hydration Process (On Page Load):
  • The application executes loadStoredArray(key, defaultArray) for each state variable.
  • If the user has saved data in localStorage, it parses and returns that data.
  • If localStorage is empty (first visit) or corrupted, it falls back to the canonical seed constants from Tier 1.
  • Sync Process (On Any Change):
  • Each state slice has a dedicated React useEffect hook.
  • Whenever state changes (e.g. user adds a transaction, pays an EMI, or contributes to a goal), saveToStorage(key, value) immediately serializes the updated state to localStorage.

items.title: External & Simulated Live Data Sources
items.text:
1. Simulated Open Banking API (src/services/fakeBankApi.js):
  2. Simulates the Indian RBI Account Aggregator (AA) framework.
  3. Allows users to link mock HDFC, SBI, ICICI, Axis, or Kotak accounts and automatically fetch bank transactions.
  4. Live Indian Market Indices (src/components/section1/MarketTickerStrip.jsx):
  5. Fetches live quotes for BSE Sensex (^BSESN), Nifty 50 (^NSEI), and Bank Nifty (^NSEBANK) via a Vite proxy to Yahoo Finance.
  6. Fetches live USD/INR exchange rates from open.er-api.com and calculates 24K Gold prices per 10 grams in INR (₹).
  7. Live Geolocation Weather (src/components/section1/WeatherWidget.jsx):
  8. Uses the browser Geolocation API to fetch live temperature and weather condition codes from the Open-Meteo REST API.

items.title: 4.1 Adding a Transaction (With EMI or Recurring Income Option)
items.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User
    participant Modal as AddTransactionModal.jsx
    participant Context as FinanceContext.jsx
    participant State as LocalStorage and State

    User->>Modal: Fills title, amount, category, date
    alt Transaction is Expense with recurring EMI option
        User->>Modal: Selects tenure (e.g. 6 months)
        User->>Modal: Clicks Save Transaction
        Modal->>Context: addTransaction(...)
        Modal->>Context: addLoan(...)
        Context->>State: Prepends transaction to ledger
        Context->>State: Prepends loan to loans array
    else Transaction is Income with recurring income option
        User->>Modal: Selects credit day (e.g. 5th of month)
        User->>Modal: Clicks Save Transaction
        Modal->>Context: addTransaction(...)
        Modal->>Context: addRecurringIncome(...)
        Context->>State: Prepends income transaction to ledger
        Context->>State: Prepends income stream to recurringIncomes array
    else Standard One-Time Transaction
        User->>Modal: Clicks Save Transaction
        Modal->>Context: addTransaction(...)
        Context->>State: Prepends transaction to ledger
    end
    Context-->>User: Auto-recalculates net balance, savings rate, and category charts

items.title: 4.2 Paying an EMI Installment (One-Click or Auto-Debit)
items.text:
flowchart LR
    A["User clicks Pay Month EMI on Loans Page"] --> B{"Already debited this month?"}
    B -->|Yes| C["Block duplicate debit to prevent double-spending"]
    B -->|No| D["Create Expense Transaction in Ledger"]
    D --> E["Title: Item Title (EMI X/Tenure)"]
    E --> F["Increment paidInstallments by 1"]
    F --> G["Set lastDebitedMonth = current YYYY-MM"]
    G --> H{"Are all installments paid?"}
    H -->|Yes| I["Set Loan Status to completed"]
    H -->|No| J["Keep Loan Status as active"]
    I --> K["Auto-update Total Remaining Debt and Net Balance"]
    J --> K

items.title: 5. The 8 Core Dashboard Views
items.text: # View Key Component File Description & Purpose 1 'overview' src/components/section1/section1.jsx Mission Control Dashboard: Dynamic time greeting, live weather preview, real-time BSE Sensex/Nifty/Gold ticker strip, 4 core KPI cards (Net Balance, Inflow, Outflow, Savings Rate), Category spending doughnut chart, last 5 ledger transactions preview, and student financial news. 2 'transactions' src/components/section2/section2.jsx Financial Ledger: Instant search bar, filter tabs (All, Income, Expenses), individual transaction rows with 50/30/20 bucket badges, delete actions, AddTransactionModal (with integrated EMI & recurring toggles), and Open Banking connection button. 3 'insights' src/components/section3/section3.jsx Cash Flow Analytics: Interactive 12-month bar chart comparing Monthly Inflow vs Outflow, multi-year comparison selector (2024, 2025, 2026), savings rate trends, and chronological multi-month prior history table. 4 'categories' src/components/section4/section4.jsx Category Spending Breakdown: Evaluates spending against the 50/30/20 budget rule (50% Needs, 30% Wants, 20% Savings), interactive category donut chart, category progress bars, and modal to add/remove custom categories. 5 'goals' src/components/section5/section5.jsx Savings Goals & Adaptive Planner: Target amounts, deadline countdowns, one-click deposits, and the AdaptiveGoalPlanner algorithm which dynamically calculates the daily micro-savings pace required to hit student goals on time. 6 'loans' src/components/loans/LoansPage.jsx EMI & Debt Payoff Center: Dedicated page for gadget, education, and personal loans. Tracks principal, interest, monthly EMI, tenure progress bars, and one-click manual EMI payments with duplicate-debit guards. 7 'subscriptions' src/components/subscriptions/SubscriptionsPage.jsx Recurring Bills & App Subscriptions: Tracks streaming (Spotify, Netflix), cloud (Google One), and utility subscriptions. Calculates monthly and annual spend run-rate, days until renewal, and category breakdown. 8 'income' src/components/income/IncomePage.jsx Monthly Recurring Income Engine: Dedicated page for predictable student inflows (allowances, internship stipends, freelance retainers, scholarships). Includes monthly deposit schedule radar and commitments coverage ratio.

items.title: 7. Core Invariants (Rules That Never Break)
items.text:
1. ₹ (INR) Currency Invariant:
  2. Every single monetary figure is formatted with the Indian Rupee symbol ₹.
  3. Never use $, €, or unformatted raw numbers in text, charts, or mock data.

  4. Standard helper: formatRupee(amount) from src/utils/financeUtils.js.

  5. Tailwind CSS v4 Standard:

  6. Uses @tailwindcss/vite with @import "tailwindcss"; in src/index.css.

  7. No legacy tailwind.config.js or postcss.config.js files are needed.

  8. In-Memory View Routing:

  9. App.jsx handles page views cleanly using React state (view: 'landing' | 'login' | 'dashboard').

  10. Keeps the bundle lightweight and eliminates external router dependencies.

  11. GSAP Cleanup Discipline:

  12. All GSAP scroll animations use gsap.context(() => { ... }) with return () => ctx.revert().

  13. Prevents memory leaks and orphaned scroll listeners.

  14. Safe LocalStorage Hydration:

  15. Every state slice uses loadStoredArray() or loadStoredItem() with try/catch.
  16. Missing or cleared storage safely loads default seed data instead of crashing.

items.title: 8. Student Project Defense / Technical Viva Q&A
Q1: Where does the app's data come from, and where does it go when a user adds a transaction?
items.text: Answer: Data starts from default seed constants in src/utils/financeUtils.js. On first launch, FinanceProvider loads these into React state and serializes them into browser localStorage. When a user adds a transaction, addTransaction updates the in-memory React state, triggering an instant UI re-render and recalculating all useMemo financial metrics. Finally, a React useEffect automatically writes the updated array back into localStorage.

items.title: Q2: Why did you choose React Context API over Redux or Zustand?
items.text: Answer: For a client-side personal finance tracker of this scale, Context API is built directly into React, requiring zero extra dependencies or bundle overhead. Coupled with custom domain hooks (useFinance, useTransactionFilters, useCashFlowMetrics), it provides clean modularity, centralized state, and straightforward debugging that any developer can understand and explain.

items.title: Q3: How does the app prevent duplicate debits for EMI and recurring income?
items.text: Answer: Each loan and recurring income tracks a lastDebitedMonth / lastCreditedMonth string formatted as YYYY-MM. When the user or system triggers a payment or credit, the handler checks if lastDebitedMonth === currentMonthKey. If true, the action is ignored, guaranteeing that the ledger is never debited or credited twice for the same calendar month.

items.title: Q4: How are calculations like the 50/30/20 budget and savings rate optimized?
items.text: Answer: Derived metrics are wrapped in React's useMemo hook with [transactions] as their dependency. This ensures that expensive array iterations and percentage calculations only execute when transactions are actually added, modified, or deleted—leaving normal UI re-renders instantaneous.

items.title: Q5: How does the application handle offline use and data persistence?
items.text: Answer: The application is 100% functional offline because all state persistence relies on browser localStorage. No server roundtrips or database connections are required for core features like transaction logging, loan payoff calculations, or savings goal tracking.
